about: Daily Tortuga Scan notes. Add a new object at the start of reports[]. Date is the local day in America/Los_Angeles. Every item needs a real source URL. See README.md.
editorial: Dial down FDA recall items unless they clearly affect people using this app, for example a product sold in Nevada or a nationally relevant clean-living product. Prefer clean-product launches, studies, and clean-living policy news.

reports.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
reports.dek: FDA pulls three solvents from food-color production, a House bill would ban every certified dye plus BHA, BHT, and TBHQ, seed-oil-free sales hit $1 billion, and two new launches skip seed oils.

items.headline: FDA revokes cancer-linked solvents used to make some food colors
items.summary: FDA is ending two remaining color-additive uses for methylene chloride and related solvents. One was methylene chloride as a thinner in the inks used to mark fruit and vegetables, which consumer groups including EWG and the Environmental Defense Fund had petitioned against. The other covers methylene chloride, ethylene dichloride, and trichloroethylene in making annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, which the color makers’ own trade group asked FDA to drop. FDA acted under the Delaney Clause, which bars ingested color additives shown to cause cancer in people or animals. The revocations take effect January 11, 2027. Annatto, paprika, and turmeric colors stay allowed; only these solvents go.

items.headline: House bills would ban all certified dyes and BHA, BHT, and TBHQ
items.summary: Rep. Nancy Mace introduced two bills. H.R. 10936 (October 29) would have HHS treat every batch-certified color additive, like Red 40 and Yellow 5, as unsafe in food, drugs, devices, and cosmetics two years after it became law. H.R. 10913 (October 26) would make food containing any BHA, BHT, or TBHQ adulterated, also after two years. Both sit in the House Energy and Commerce Committee with no hearing or vote scheduled, so nothing changes yet. FDA’s current push to remove the six remaining synthetic dyes is still voluntary, with an end-of-2027 target, and Red 3 is out of food after January 15, 2027. Tortuga already docks BHA, BHT, and TBHQ.

items.headline: Seed-oil-free product sales reach $1 billion
items.summary: Morning Brew, citing a Bloomberg report, says sales of products labeled seed-oil-free rose 72 percent to about $1 billion over the past year. Health brands and big snack makers, including PepsiCo and Utz, are adding chips and snacks cooked in alternatives such as beef tallow. A seed-oil-free claim is still only one check: scan the rest of the label for gums, natural flavors, and conventional glyphosate-prone crops.

items.headline: Stellar Snacks bakes a Pretzel Braids line with olive oil, only at Sprouts
items.summary: Stellar Snacks, based in Carson City, Nevada, launched Pretzel Braids Baked with Olive Oil, a six-flavor seed-oil-free line sold only at Sprouts Farmers Market nationwide. Two flavors are new, Elote Loco and Spicy Flame, alongside Maui Monk, Bold & Herby, Cinnamon Dolce, and French Dijon. The original braids at Target, Kroger, and Costco are a separate line, so check which bag you grab. Pretzels are wheat, so look for organic flour on the label before calling it a full pass.
items.sourceName: Recipes ’n Cooking, citing the brand’s press release

items.headline: Incredifulls rolls out frozen PB&J cups made without seed oils
items.summary: Incredifulls, the Pizza Cupcake brand, is launching Paw Patrol Peanut Butter & Jelly Cups nationally: peanut butter and jelly baked inside a sourdough-brioche crust, sold frozen in boxes of four for a suggested $5.99 to $6.99. The company says they are made without seed oils, artificial colors, or high-fructose corn syrup, with 5 g of protein each. We haven’t seen the full ingredient list yet, so sugar and flour quality are unknown until it’s scanned.

items.headline: Pumpkin seeds and pumpkin seed oil didn’t beat a plain low-cholesterol diet
items.summary: A randomized trial in the Irish Journal of Medical Science followed 89 overweight adults with high blood lipids for four weeks on a low-cholesterol diet, adding 30 g a day of pumpkin seeds, 15 g a day of pumpkin seed oil, or nothing. Cholesterol, LDL, and liver enzymes fell in all three groups. Triglycerides dropped only in the two pumpkin groups, but the difference between groups wasn’t statistically significant. The authors say more research is needed. It’s small and short, so the takeaway is that the diet change did most of the work.

items.headline: Fresh To You breakfast biscuit sandwiches recalled for Listeria
items.summary: Fresh & Ready Foods of Renton, Washington, is recalling 2,414 Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches (4.6 oz, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, Fresh Thru 11/07 to 11/19). The biscuit came from a CH Guenther & Son recall. They went to break rooms, vending machines, and cafeterias in Oregon and Washington only, so Nevada shelves aren’t on the list. No illnesses reported. Don’t eat it; the company offers refunds.

items.headline: Mexico drops Red 3 and starts a new food-additive rulebook this month
items.summary: Mexico’s Health Ministry removed Red 3 (erythrosine) from foods, drinks, and supplements in May, giving companies 24 months to reformulate. A separate agreement replacing its 2012 additive rules starts this month, with sources giving dates from November 13 to late November. Some colorants get numeric limits for the first time, and additives must be listed by name on labels.

reports.title: Monday, November 9, 2026
reports.dek: First Tortuga Scan daily note. Recalls and public lab alerts from the past week, in our words. Older studies — avocado oil, cocoa metals, infant rice arsenic — are filed under Lab tests, not as today’s headlines.

items.headline: Brad’s kale chips recalled after thallium testing
items.summary: Snack Right Super Foods, which sells Brad’s Raw Chips, is recalling about 25,000 bags of Brad’s Plant Based Crunchy Kale (2 oz) and Veggie Chips Kale (3 oz). FDA posted the notice on November 3. The chips went out through KeHE and UNFI between October and December 2025, and best-by dates run into February 2027. California’s health department tested store samples in the Sacramento area after one person had high thallium, and FDA then told the company. The notice says drying removes about 85 to 90 percent of the water and concentrates metal already in the kale. It does not publish a thallium number. The company is not giving refunds. Don’t eat the listed lots.

items.headline: Once Upon a Farm recalls Tractor Wheels toddler bars
items.summary: Once Upon a Farm is recalling every lot and flavor of Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars. FDA published the company notice on November 2; the company dated it October 30. The firm says three choking complaints were reported to FDA and that no injuries have been reported to the company. FDA’s own advisory, updated November 3, says it has several reports of toddlers about 1.5 to 2.5 years old whose airway was fully blocked, and that some incidents needed emergency care and hospital observation. Both say the bar can turn into a dry, sticky mass when chewed. Other Once Upon a Farm products are not part of this recall. The company says it is reformulating. Don’t serve the bars; take them back or throw them out.

items.headline: USDA alert: Betterballen snacks left sesame and fish off the label
items.summary: On November 6, USDA’s food safety service issued a public health alert for frozen Betterballen Bami Rolls, Saté Kroketten, and Bitterballen. The labels don’t say sesame. The beef bitterballen also contain anchovy in the Worcestershire sauce and don’t say fish. A recall was not asked for because the products are no longer for sale, but some may still be in freezers. They were made October 15, 16, and 27, 2026, sold online by Lowlands House, and may have been sold at a festival and farmers market in Greer, South Carolina. No illnesses were confirmed. Throw them out or take them back.

items.headline: FDA lists Wise Wife cinnamon at 2.118 ppm lead
items.summary: On November 4, FDA added a Wise Wife ground cinnamon to its public alert after the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station measured 2.118 ppm lead. The jar is 110 g, UPC 0688474302754, best before April 25, 2027, and was recalled October 29. The same FDA table lists an older Wise Wife UPC at 2.49 ppm. FDA says those levels are much lower than the 2,270 to 5,110 ppm lead in cinnamon from the 2023 WanaBana applesauce recall, and still says to throw the listed cinnamon out. Figures and links are in Lab tests.
